records.query: tic tac toe two player online no account
records.problem: I want a clean two-player tic-tac-toe I can play hot-seat in one browser tab with friends in the same room, with no account and no network.
searchQueries: play tic tac toe same device
solutionWeaknesses: forced online matchmaking for a couch game
no undo of an accidental tap
userFailures: An accidental double-tap places two marks before either player notices whose turn it was.
A finished board has no rematch affordance so they refresh and lose the score streak.
Color-only X/O styling fails for a colorblind player sharing the same screen.
They expect an optional AI opponent and the empty second seat just sits idle with no explanation.

records.problem: I want Connect Four for two players on one device, with win detection and a reset that does not require a page reload.
solutionWeaknesses: matchmaking when both players are on one couch
touch targets too small on phones
userFailures: A disc is dropped in the wrong column because the hover highlight lagged behind the finger.
A diagonal win is missed by the detector when the board is full of near-misses.
Undo reverts two plies instead of one after a mis-tap, and the turn indicator disagrees with the board.
Landscape mode clips the top row on a short phone and the winning cell is off-screen.

records.query: chess tac toe hybrid board game
records.problem: I want Chess-Tac-Toe (chess piece movement constraints on a tic-tac-toe style win) as a local hot-seat puzzle game with clear legal-move hints.
solutionWeaknesses: rules pages never ship a playable board
userFailures: A player places a piece on an occupied square because the UI reused plain tic-tac-toe click handling.
Knight-move legality is checked from the wrong origin after a capture variant the ruleset does not allow.
Win detection fires on three-in-a-row while a chess-check rule the house uses is ignored, with no mode toggle.
New players cannot tell whose turn it is because piece color and turn banner disagree after undo.

records.problem: I want Quantum Tic-Tac-Toe with entanglement and collapse rules playable hot-seat in the browser, so the weird rules are enforced by the tool instead of argued over.
solutionWeaknesses: demos assume you already know the collapse rules
no step-through of why a collapse fired
userFailures: A player marks two classical cells thinking a spooky mark is already collapsed, and the board accepts an illegal classical move.
Collapse order is ambiguous when two cycles resolve and the tool picks one silently.
The entanglement graph is never shown, so disputes about which marks are linked cannot be settled.
Undo after a collapse cannot restore the prior superposition and the match has to be abandoned.
